result.title: MultiFlow: Vision-Driven Multimodal fMRI Encoding via Stimulus-Informed Source Flow Matching
result.comment: 17 pages, 7 figures, 7 tables. Accepted at the British Machine Vision Conference (BMVC) 2026
result.summary: Current fMRI encoding models frame prediction as deterministic regression, yet identical stimuli evoke a distribution of neural responses (arising from physiological noise, hemodynamic variability, and cognitive fluctuations) that a single point estimate cannot capture. This work introduces MultiFlow, a generative fMRI encoding framework based on Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) and a formulation termed Stimulus-Informed Source Flow Matching (SISFM). SISFM generalises CFM by conditioning the source distribution on the stimulus: a learnable temporal convolution shapes the source mean with an HRF-length receptive field, while a variance head shrinks its scale, shortening the expected transport path. SISFM is instantiated with a Diffusion Transformer (DiT-X) decoder parameterising the velocity field, with sub-layer Attention Residuals, heterogeneous fusion of ten frozen vision, audio, language, and audiovisual backbones, and per-subject Yeo-network heads. On the Algonauts 2025 dataset, a single MultiFlow checkpoint recovers most of the benefit of large deterministic ensembles: it trails the 1000-model TRIBE ensemble in-distribution by 0.003 PCC (0.3163 vs. 0.3195), and the strongest in- and out-of-distribution ensembles (VIBE-20, MedARC-50) by 0.010 and 0.009 PCC, using a single trained model rather than an ensemble of 20-1000. The same checkpoint also provides stimulus-conditioned uncertainty estimates and sample-based diversity.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MultiFlow，一个基于条件流匹配的生成式 fMRI 编码框架：用 SISFM 让源分布以刺激为条件（可学习时间卷积塑造源均值、方差头缩短传输路径），以 DiT-X 解码器、十个冻结视觉/音频/语言骨干的异构融合实现单模型编码，并给出刺激条件下的不确定性与样本多样性。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文指出同一刺激对应一个神经响应分布而非单点估计，「刺激条件下源分布 + 方差头缩短传输路径」可能为 latent 推理状态的初始化与分布建模提供线索，多样本采样与不确定性估计或可供核查「多种 latent 假设」的取舍与评价，但属较远领域，迁移性需自行判断。
